_meta.description: Authoritative Australian tax and wage constants for FY2026-27. Every figure is sourced from official ATO or Fair Work Commission pages and stored with provenance. Do NOT edit values without updating source_url and retrieved_on.
_meta.maintainer_note: See README.md in this directory for the update procedure.

rate.label: GST rate (goods and services tax)
rate.notes: GST is a broad-based tax of 10% on most goods, services and other items sold or consumed in Australia. Rate unchanged since GST introduction 1 July 2000.

registration_threshold_aud.label: GST registration turnover threshold (standard businesses)
registration_threshold_aud.notes: Non-profit organisations have a higher threshold of $150,000.

calc_method.label: GST calculation method for price including GST
calc_method.notes: To find the GST component of a GST-inclusive price, divide by 11. To add GST to a GST-exclusive price, multiply by 1.1.

G1.label: G1 - Total sales (GST-inclusive sales for the period)
G1.description: Report the total of all your taxable, GST-free and input-taxed sales. Include the GST amount in the total.
G1.calc: Sum of all sales including GST where applicable
G1.notes: Simpler BAS reporting method. G1 is the only sales figure required under Simpler BAS (introduced 1 July 2017 for small businesses with turnover under $10M).

1A.label: 1A - GST on sales (GST collected on taxable sales)
1A.description: Report the GST included in the price of your taxable sales. Under Simpler BAS, calculated as G1 divided by 11 (for fully taxable sales).
1A.calc: Taxable sales GST amount = taxable sales value / 11
1A.notes: This is the GST liability on sales. Remitted to the ATO.

1B.label: 1B - GST on purchases (GST credits claimed on business purchases)
1B.description: Report the GST included in the price of business purchases for which you are claiming a GST credit (input tax credit).
1B.calc: Sum of GST on creditable acquisitions (purchase price / 11 for fully taxable purchases)
1B.notes: This is the input tax credit. Reduces the GST you owe. Net GST payable = 1A minus 1B.

guarantee_rate.label: Super guarantee rate (SG rate)
guarantee_rate.notes: Rate applies from 1 July 2026. Unchanged from FY2025-26 (12%). Previous rates: 11.5% FY2024-25, 11% FY2023-24. With Payday Super from 1 July 2026, employers pay super per payday (not quarterly).

max_contribution_base_annual_aud.label: Maximum super contribution base FY2026-27 (annual, from 1 July 2026)
max_contribution_base_annual_aud.notes: Maximum annual qualifying earnings for which employer must pay SG. From 1 July 2026 this is an annual figure (previously quarterly). Formula: concessional cap x 100 / charge %.

concessional_contributions_cap_aud.label: General concessional contributions cap FY2026-27
concessional_contributions_cap_aud.notes: Indexed via AWOTE. Previous cap was $30,000 (FY2024-25 and FY2025-26). Concessional contributions include employer SG, salary sacrifice, and personal deductible contributions.

income_tax._note: FY2026-27 resident tax brackets had not been separately published by the ATO as of 2026-06-28. The brackets below are the FY2025-26 rates, which are the most recent published on the ATO tax rates page (last updated 1 June 2026). The same brackets applied for FY2024-25. See README.md for details.

resident_brackets.label: Australian resident income tax brackets FY2025-26 (most recent published as at 2026-06-28)
resident_brackets.notes: These brackets do NOT include the Medicare levy of 2%. The ATO page title says 'income years from 2026' but the most recent explicitly labelled table is FY2025-26. FY2024-25 used the same brackets. The ATO publishes FY2026-27 brackets separately when the income year begins.

rate.label: Medicare levy rate (standard rate for full-year residents)
rate.notes: The Medicare levy is 2% of taxable income. It is paid in addition to income tax. Reductions and exemptions may apply for low-income earners and certain other circumstances.

rate.label: FBT rate (fringe benefits tax) for FBT years ending 31 March 2023 to 31 March 2027
rate.notes: The FBT year runs from 1 April to 31 March. The 47% rate applies for FBT years ending 31 March 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 and 2027. This covers the FBT year ending 31 March 2027 (which spans FY2026-27).

gross_up_rate_type1.label: FBT Type 1 gross-up rate (where provider is entitled to a GST credit)
gross_up_rate_type1.notes: Used when the benefit provider can claim GST input tax credits on the benefit.

gross_up_rate_type2.label: FBT Type 2 gross-up rate (where provider is not entitled to a GST credit)
gross_up_rate_type2.notes: Used when the benefit provider cannot claim GST input tax credits.

national_minimum_wage_hourly_aud.label: National Minimum Wage (per hour, from 1 July 2026)
national_minimum_wage_hourly_aud.notes: Announced by the Fair Work Commission following the 2026 Annual Wage Review (decision published 28 May 2026). Applies from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026. Previous rate: $24.95/hour (FY2025-26). The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement.

national_minimum_wage_weekly_aud.label: National Minimum Wage (per week, from 1 July 2026)
national_minimum_wage_weekly_aud.notes: Weekly rate based on 38 ordinary hours. Announced by the Fair Work Commission in the 2026 Annual Wage Review. Previous rate: $948/week (FY2025-26).

casual_loading_rate.label: Minimum casual loading rate (National Employment Standards)
casual_loading_rate.notes: Minimum 25% casual loading on the base rate of pay, set by the Fair Work Act 2009 s.96 (National Employment Standards). This rate applies to award/agreement-free casual employees. Individual awards may specify different rates. Note: the FWO website has been reorganized; direct casual loading page URLs return 404. The loading is referenced on the minimum wages hub page and is set in legislation.
